Date: 08/24/2026
Company: SAP

We help the world run better
At SAP, we keep it simple: you bring your best to us, and we'll bring out the best in you. We're builders touching over 20 industries and 80% of global commerce, and we need your unique talents to help shape what's next. The work is challenging – but it matters. Meet your team

SAP Global Security & Cloud Compliance’s mission is to manage security and compliance risks for SAP by

reinforcing a security- and compliance-first culture and by aligning people, processes, and technology to protect

customer business operations, the company, and its employees.

Within this mission, the Human Security Risk & Compliance function is evolving from a training-centric model

toward a human-centric risk & compliance model that systematically identifies, mitigates, monitors, and reports

on human-centric security risks across SAP.

This role sits at the intersection of software security, secure development enablement, and Human Risk

Management, helping SAP embed security into engineering roles at scale through practical, measurable, and

business-relevant approaches.

What you’ll do

As a Community Manager in this role, you will deliver on the following key responsibilities:

Take ownership of SAP's internal security community, its members, cadence, formats, and channels, ensuring it remains active, welcoming, and valuable to security professionals, engineers, and interested colleagues alike

Analyze the current state of the community and establish a clear, measurable baseline of community health (active participation, contribution, engagement, retention) as the foundation for targeted, evidence-based improvement

Sustain and nurture the existing community: maintain its identity, relationships, and rhythm of activities, and act as a reliable point of contact and connector for members

- Design and run community activities that foster engagement and knowledge exchange (e.g., meetups, brown-bag sessions, community events, knowledge-sharing formats, champion/ambassador initiatives), in close coordination with technical subject matter experts

- Maintain clear documentation of the community's operating model, relationships, and ongoing initiatives to ensure continuity and a smooth handover at the end of the assignment
- In this role, you will be expected to:
- Grow measurable, sustained engagement within the security community and strengthen its role as a channel for security culture and security-first behavior
- Translate an analytical view of community health into practical initiatives with visible results
- Collaborate with security subject matter experts, enablement colleagues, and engineering stakeholders to keep community activities technically credible and relevant
- Operate as a dependable steward of the community, building trust with members and ensuring continuity throughout the assignment

What you bring

Bachelor's / Master's degree in a relevant discipline (e.g., Communications, Business, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Business Informatics), or equivalent practical experience

- Proven experience in community management, engagement, or comparable roles building and sustaining active professional or technical communities
- Sufficient security literacy to engage credibly with security professionals and engineers, able to follow technical discussion, understand the domain, and earn the trust of a technically demanding audience (a security background is a plus, but this is not a hands-on engineering role)
- Strong facilitation, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to connect people and motivate voluntary participation
- Experience planning and running events, programs, or engagement formats, and measuring their impact through meaningful metrics rather than vanity numbers
- Analytical mindset: able to assess the current state of a community objectively and turn findings into practical, prioritized action
- Ability to work effectively with developers, architects, security professionals, and cross-functional stakeholders
- High level of motivation, ownership, and reliability, together with fluent English language skills. German is a plus.

You have several years of hands-on experience in software architecture and development, ideally in the utilities or energy industry. You have a deep understanding of the technical landscape underpinning German energy market communication — from message exchange to smart meter gateway integration — and you stay informed about relevant regulatory and technology trends. Based on your architectural expertise, your knowledge of cloud-native patterns, and your strong analytical skills, you design solutions that are both technically sound and valuable to customers.

You will be part of the Industry AI unit for Energy and Natural Resources, a team focused on turning Industry AI opportunities in the ENR space into measurable customer value.
In this role, you’ll help raise engineering standards beyond your immediate responsibility by driving architectural best practices, fostering an AI-powered development culture, and enabling your team to deliver with confidence and speed.
If you want to shape the technical foundation of solutions that run critical energy infrastructure and are ready to take Industry AI for ENR from architecture to AI-supported implementation, this role is a great fit for you.
Key competencies in this role include agentic engineering, agentic orchestration, AI-assisted engineering, cloud architecture, cloud security architecture, CI/CD, evaluation and benchmark engineering, scalability design, semantic retrieval, systems thinking, and technical leadership. In addition, you have experience in the daily use of agentic AI as well as in promoting AI adoption in engineering organizations.
Other skills used in this role: Collaboration, Complex Problem Solving, Creative Thinking, Effective Communication, Learning Agility, Agentic AI Day-to-Day Practice, AI Adoption Capability, AI Output Quality Assurance, Context Engineering, AI-Assisted Automation and Prototyping.

At the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law, scholars pursue research relating to fundamental issues and current developments in the areas of public international law, European Union law, and the constitutional and administrative law of individual states, together with numerous visiting scholars from all over the world. In its fields, our library is the largest in Europe and one of the most comprehensive in the world.

The newly established Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER), headed by Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, invites applications for two

Research Fellow positions (Doctoral Researchers) (x/f/m)

with a preferred starting date of 1 January 2027 (the positions are funded for three years)

The Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER) investigates how global order is transformed as states - particularly great and middle powers - pursue competing visions of the principles, rules and institutions that structure international relations amid intensifying geopolitical rivalry. The group conceptualizes these processes as constellations of global (dis)ordering through which states seek to advance their visions of order by creating, reshaping, connecting, bypassing, or disengaging from international institutions, building new formal or ad hoc institutional arrangements, and strategically leveraging economic and technological interdependence. DISORDER examines how such constellations emerge across the fields of security, economy, and technology, and what forms of global order they produce, transform, or erode.

Job description

The successful candidates will develop independent doctoral dissertation projects within the framework of the Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER). Their research should contribute to the group’s broader inquiry into how states pursue competing visions of global order through international institutions and how these processes reshape global order across different issue areas.

Possible orientations of the doctoral projects include:

- an actor-centred perspective, examining how a particular great or middle power pursues its vision of global order across different issue areas institutional settings; or
- a domain-centred perspective, comparing how different states interact with and reshape international institutions within a particular field, such as security, economy, or technology.

Potential empirical cases may include, but are not limited to, the United States, China, Russia, India, Brazil, Japan, and other international actors such as the European Union.

The doctoral researchers will:

- develop and conduct an original PhD project that contributes to the conceptual and empirical agenda of the DISORDER research group;
- conduct empirical research using qualitative methods such as process tracing, qualitative content and discourse analysis, and semi-structured interviews;
- contribute to the comparative and collaborative research activities of the group;
- participate in research group meetings, workshops, conferences, and other academic activities;
- present research findings at international conferences and prepare publications for peer-reviewed academic outlets;
- contribute to the organization of workshops, conferences, and other activities of the research group and the MPIL.

Your profile

- An excellent Master’s degree or equivalent in Political Science, with a specialization in International Relations or Foreign Policy Analysis
- A strong research interest in global order, international institutions, and great- and middle-power politics, including their foreign policies
- A substantive interest in one or more of the group’s empirical issue areas (security, economy, and technology)
- A strong interest in qualitative research and familiarity with relevant research methods
- Excellent written and spoken English
- Additional language skills and country- or region-specific expertise relevant to the proposed doctoral project are considered assets
- The ability to conduct independent research while contributing actively to a collaborative research environment

We offer

- An attractive and international work environment with an unparalleled research infrastructure and a good working atmosphere
- A varied, responsible and team-orientated job
- Remuneration in accordance with the guidelines of the MPG funding agreements (65 per cent of EG13, TVöD-Bund)
- Access to our world-leading library and a multitude of databases
- A workplace that is easy to reach by public transport and free employee parking spaces

jobs.description:
About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. Job description

In order to support Earth Observation & Science projects within Space Systems, Airbus Defence and Space in Ottobrunn is looking for an

Optical Architect (d/f/m)

You will join a multicultural team of engineers specialized in the development of optical (sub-)systems working for Earth Observation & Science projects within Space Systems. These developments cover instruments for ESA, CNES, DLR and EU programmes across the spectral range from ultraviolet to thermal infrared. Examples include LIDARs (ATLID, MERLIN), Multi-Spectral Instruments (Sentinel-2 MSI, Sentinel-4, Sentinel-5) from the Copernicus programme, infrared instruments (LSTM, TRISHNA), meteorological instruments (IASI-NG and METimage) embarked on MetOp-SG, instruments for scientific missions like EUCLID, cameras embarked on LEO and GEO satellites, and national programmes.

This role is also available with reduced weekly hours and an adapted scope of tasks.

Your location

Our site is just a stone's throw away from Munich, the beautiful capital of Bavaria.

Are you into sports and other outdoor activities? The Alps and Lake Starnberg are within an hour’s reach, offering a multitude of recreational options.

Our Benefits for You

- Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, such as company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g., bike leasing), or corporate discounts with partner companies in accordance with our current guidelines.
- Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement (35-hour week); work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities.
- Growth Made Easy: Excellent professional development opportunities and international, group-wide career perspectives.
- Feel Good at Work: On-site company doctor; comprehensive health programs (sports courses, preventive care, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, and local childcare facilities at selected locations.
- Diversity Connects: Work in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, mutual support, and inclusion are part of our DNA.

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Define and develop optical subsystem architecture and verification strategies for space-borne instruments in project phases B2, C, and D following defined processes.
- Act as the main technical contact point for optical domain matters, supporting systems engineers on technological, design, verification, risk, cost, and schedule aspects.
- Perform optical design and analysis, including stray light analysis, optical layout, tolerances, and stray light, thermal, and optical performance (STOP) budget allocations.
- Coordinate optical subsystem engineering and Assembly, Integration, and Testing (AIT) activities across multidisciplinary teams (Mechanical, Thermal, Electrical, Detection-chain, Cleanliness).
- Derive, consolidate, and maintain optical subsystem requirements in alignment with higher-level specifications (e.g., SRD, IRD) and verification plans.
- Oversee subcontracted optical equipment procurement, reviewing data packages and test plans to ensure on-time, on-cost, and on-quality delivery.
- Contribute to future programmes (phase 0 or A/B1), support internal/external R&D proposals for new optical technologies, and participate in lessons-learnt exchanges.

- Master's degree or PhD in Physics, Optical Engineering
- Proven multi-year experience in optical instrumentation or optical sensors, ideally for space applications
- Solid experience in optical layout, design, tolerance, and STOP analysis, including maintenance of optical allocations/budgets.
- Proficiency with commercial optical design software (e.g., Code V, Zemax, FRED) and programming languages (e.g., Matlab, Python).
- Sound technical knowledge of optical components (e.g., mirrors, photonics, gratings, fibers, lasers, coatings) and space equipment alignment/testing strategies.
- Strong communication skills, collaborative problem-solving approach, and experience in managing suppliers or subcontractors.
- Professional working proficiency in English; knowledge of German is beneficial.

Take your career to a new level and apply online now!

The German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) is one of Europe’s largest cancer research centers. “Research for a life without cancer" is the mission of our world-class scientists and all our team members.

We investigate how cancer develops, identify cancer risk factors and search for new cancer prevention strategies. We develop new methods with which tumors can be diagnosed more precisely and cancer patients can be treated more successfully. Every contribution counts – whether in research, administration or infrastructure. This is what makes our daily work so meaningful and exciting.

Our Junior Research Group "Epithelium Microbiome Interactions" (headed by Dr. Jens Puschhof) is seeking, starting at the earliest date possible, a Administrative Lab Technician.

In the EMIL group, we study how bacteria contribute to cancer development, metastasis, and treatment response. Our team includes cancer researchers, tissue engineers, microbiologists, and bioinformaticians working together to help patients by deciphering the functional impacts of bacteria in human tumors.
Using tissue samples from patients, we isolate bacterial strains and create organoids. These models can be combined with additional features of the human gut on USB stick-sized devices, “organ chips”, for detailed studies. We transplant organoid-bacteria mixtures into mouse models to study their migration and interaction in a whole-body context.
In our unique biobank at DKFZ, we characterize both tumor organoids and tumor-resident bacterial strains through whole genome sequencing, fluorescence microscopy, and other cutting-edge methods. Based on the diverse data obtained, we develop hypotheses about how specific bacterial species might influence tumors. With our broad portfolio of patient-derived models, our main focus lies on testing these relationships. Through close collaborations with clinical partners, we work towards the rapid translation of our findings into new microbiome-based strategies for the detection, prevention, and treatment of cancer.

- Organization and coordination of day-to-day laboratory operations, including inventory management, procurement, equipment maintenance, shipping, and logistics
- Coordination of occupational safety, biosafety, and laboratory safety procedures, including support with regulatory documentation and internal inspections
- Organization and quality control of shared consumables, reagents, and laboratory spaces
- Experimental and administrative management of the organoid biobank and bacterial strain collection
- Performance and coordination of key laboratory assays, particularly genotyping and mycoplasma testing
- Onboarding, practical instruction, and supervision of students and new group members
- Communication and coordination with suppliers, service providers, internal DKFZ units, and external collaboration partners

Your Profile

- Very good practical knowledge of biological and/or molecular biology laboratory work and laboratory organization

- Independent, structured, and reliable working style with strong organizational skills

- Very good written and spoken English and German

We Offer

Are you interested?

Then become part of the DKFZ and join us in contributing to a life without cancer!

Job description

**Ground Test Engineer (d/f/m) - Engineering Ground Test on Aircraft **

You will join the Ground Test team, which is part of the Flight Test Center of AIRBUS Helicopters Germany. Our team performs development, certification, and qualification testing activities on aircraft on ground. It comprises the domains electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), avionics and vehicle mission systems, vibrations, and acoustics.
Our main goal is to ensure system maturity for by making the bridge between avionic/vehicle rigs and flight tests. In order to do that we optimize integration and test sequence in close relationship with design office, simulation, rigs, flight-test crews, and prototype shops. Finally, we show compliance with regulations specifications or certification/qualification requirements, in order to get our aircraft certified.

Your location:

At our Donauwörth site, located on the banks of the river Danube, we develop helicopters from the initial idea to the airworthy product. Watch them take off and touch down on our own on-site test airfield.

- Being responsible for ground test activities mainly for EMC, and in addition for vibration and acoustic tests for civil and military platforms

Job description

The A400M is a versatile European tactical airlifter that bridges the gap between traditional transport aircraft and strategic airlift capabilities. It stands as a symbol of industrial excellence and collaborative defense capability.

Be part of this journey and join our team to shape the future of A400M simulation! We develop advanced simulation software for the A400M programme, ranging from high-fidelity Full Flight Simulators (FFS) for pilot training to advanced test facilities for avionics integration and certification. We support the A400M Military Test and Support Facility (MTSF) by providing simulation models that enable the verification and certification of avionics at software, equipment, and system levels. Our work ensures that aircraft updates are accurately represented in both training and test environments, utilizing a tech stack centered on C/C++.

As a Junior Software Engineer in our MTSF team, you will be responsible for the full lifecycle of simulation solutions. You will translate high‑level operational and system requirements from a variety of stakeholders into robust simulation models, design and define the necessary simulation interfaces, develop and test complex models, and drive the successful release and deployment of those models. Throughout the process you will guarantee high‑quality delivery and provide support during customer‑acceptance activities.
